label: Future Forms
outcome: Lo studente sceglie tra will, be going to e Present Continuous for future partendo dal significato comunicativo: decisione immediata/previsione, piano-intenzione o previsione basata su evidenza, accordo futuro già organizzato.
must_master: will for neutral predictions/opinions at programme level
be going to for prior plans and intentions
be going to for evidence-based predictions
Present Continuous for fixed future arrangements
choose will / going to / Present Continuous from meaning and degree of organisation
correct am/is/are going to + base verb structure
correct am/is/are + verb-ing structure for arrangements
distinguish a Present Continuous future arrangement from an action happening now through future context

scope_boundary.present_simple_timetables: Do not add Present Simple for timetables to this core topic unless a student's school programme explicitly requires it; the curriculum outcome here is will/going to/Present Continuous.
scope_boundary.advanced_future: Do not introduce Future Continuous, Future Perfect or be about to.
scope_boundary.conditionals: Do not teach future time clauses or conditional structures here even though a diagnostic code exists for them.
scope_boundary.offers_promises: A small will offer/promise example is acceptable when useful, but instant decisions and predictions remain the core will meanings.
scope_boundary.arrangements: Present Continuous future examples must include enough future context to distinguish them from actions happening now.

decision_model: Decision made at the moment of speaking → will.
Prediction/opinion without present physical evidence → will at this level.
Plan or intention decided before speaking → be going to.
Prediction based on visible/current evidence → be going to.
Fixed personal arrangement with concrete organisation such as time/place/person → Present Continuous for future.
After choosing the meaning, build the selected form correctly.

italian_learner_risks.risk: using will for every future meaning
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: I've already decided: I will study medicine next year.
italian_learner_risks.target: I'm going to study medicine next year.

italian_learner_risks.risk: using going to without a base verb
confusing a fixed arrangement with a vague intention
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: using the same form regardless of whether a meeting is merely intended or already booked
italian_learner_risks.target: use Present Continuous when the arrangement is concretely organised

italian_learner_risks.risk: reading a future Present Continuous as happening now
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: interpreting I'm meeting Luca at six tomorrow as a current meeting
italian_learner_risks.target: use the future time context to identify the arrangement

context_bank: a phone rings and someone decides to answer
a prediction based on personal opinion
dark clouds or an obviously unstable object as visible evidence
a plan chosen before the conversation
a booked doctor, teacher, train-station or friend meeting
weekend plans that range from intention to fixed arrangement
short text-message exchanges where the future meaning changes during the conversation
school-style mixed future-form completion with unambiguous context

requirements: teach communicative meaning before form labels
contrast instant decision with prior plan
contrast opinion prediction with evidence-based prediction
show the form of all three structures
five scaffolded graded checks after teaching
at least one item must require both form choice and correct construction
mix all three future forms rather than blocking them into separate mini-worksheets
include one dialogue with an instant decision
include one connected mini-context with more than one future form
do not make tomorrow/next week mechanically determine the answer
no teaching or coaching during the task
include one controlled production or translation task

quality_rejections: a worksheet where tomorrow automatically means going to
will used as the default answer for every future sentence
ambiguous contexts where intention and fixed arrangement are equally defensible
an arrangement example with no future time or organisational context
teaching Present Simple timetables, Future Continuous or Future Perfect inside this topic
conditionals or future time clauses introduced before their own curriculum topic
more than two consecutive isolated form-only questions
difficulty created by vocabulary rather than future meaning
